scenes.headline: How GEM-4D teaches a video model geometry
scenes.sub: A training branch that is thrown away before the robot ever uses it
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nico! GEM-4D is a video world model for robot arms that learns 3D geometry in training, then sheds the part that taught it.

scenes.title: Video in, actions out
scenes.sub: A world model, then a separate program that measures it
scenes.say: Chapter one. Video in, actions out.

scenes.title: A video model as a robot policy
scenes.say: The recipe: don't learn actions directly. Imagine the future, then measure it.

items.say: A world model takes the first frame and an instruction, and generates the next few seconds.
An extractor finds the gripper in each frame and lifts it into 3D with estimated depth.
Inverse kinematics turns that path into joint commands.

steps.term: Correspondence: same 3D point, matched across frames
steps.say: Here is the trap. On the left, five generated frames: the gripper steps right by the same few pixels. On the right, what they mean in 3D.
Make the scene deeper, and the reach grows. The frames do not change.
Or the camera panned, and the gripper barely moved. Same frames again.
Now the real failure. Each frame implies its own depth. Every frame looks fine, but in 3D the reach zigzags, and the arm would follow.
A pixel loss cannot tell these apart. A model with one consistent geometry can.

scenes.title: Where a point lands in the next frame
scenes.text: p' = K [ R D K^-1 p + T + dX ]
scenes.say: The paper writes it down. Where a pixel lands in the next frame depends on four things.

parts.note: the camera's rotation, then its translation
parts.say: How the camera rotated and moved.
And how the point itself moved, its scene flow.
Get those four right inside the model, and every correspondence is fixed.

scenes.title: A branch it will lose
scenes.sub: Teach the middle of the network, then cut the teacher away
scenes.say: Chapter two. A branch it will lose.

scenes.text: Make one middle block of the video model carry enough geometry that a small side network can predict a frozen depth model's features from it.
scenes.mark: predict a frozen depth model's features
scenes.term: Geometry teacher: a frozen depth and pose model
scenes.say: Here's the idea. Bolt a small network onto a middle block of the video model, and make it predict what a frozen depth model sees. It only succeeds if that block encodes geometry.

steps.say: Along the bottom, an ordinary video transformer learns to denoise the clip.
Along the top, a frozen geometry model turns the clip into features, noised and half masked, for a Geometry DiT to denoise.
Its only view of the scene is this arrow: the video model's features. So its gradient pushes geometry into them.

scenes.title: From depth features to a geometry latent

steps.term: Depth Anything 3: the code's frozen teacher
steps.say: In the released code, the teacher is Depth Anything 3. Its twelfth layer gives a thousand and twenty-four channels.
A frozen random projection squeezes that to two hundred and fifty-six.
Every four frames are averaged: forty-nine become thirteen.
Then sixteen channels, shaped exactly like a video latent.
Half its tokens are masked, and the geometry loss is weighted by zero point zero three.
One training step. The clip goes through the video transformer, forty blocks, and gets the usual video loss.
The frozen teacher's features are the target for the four-block Geometry DiT.

steps.note: the branch reads block 20 and never writes back
steps.say: It reads block twenty through cross-attention, and the gradient flows back. Nothing flows the other way.

steps.note: at inference, only the video DiT runs
steps.say: After training, the teacher and the branch are deleted. A plain video model ships.

scenes.title: Parameters, 14B release
scenes.note: trained together, the branch is absent from the shipped weights
scenes.say: The cost: on the released model, the video transformer is sixteen point three nine billion parameters. The branch adds one point seven three billion in training, and nothing when generating.

scenes.title: From frames to a gripper
scenes.sub: The extractor, built from off-the-shelf models
scenes.say: Chapter three. From frames to a gripper.

steps.term: Inverse dynamics: reading actions from frames
steps.say: Then the extractor. A vision-language model and SAM 2 find the object and the gripper, and a pose model fits the gripper's shape.
A point tracker follows the gripper, and finds it again when tracking suddenly drops.
Bad poses are repaired, a grasp is chosen, and inverse kinematics makes the motion. This part is not released.

scenes.title: Does it hold up?
scenes.sub: Better geometry, and a headline that needs reading
scenes.say: Chapter four. Does it hold up?

steps.say: TesserAct outputs depth directly. Lift its frames to 3D, and the arm smears.
GEM-4D's frames, lifted the same way, hold together.

scenes.title: Point-cloud error on RLBench
scenes.say: On RLBench, where depth is exact, the point-cloud error falls to less than half the best baseline's.

scenes.title: Seven RLBench tasks, mean success
scenes.say: The headline: twenty-two point seven to seventy-five point one percent on seven tasks, with TesserAct's videos run through GEM-4D's own extractor.

items.say: There is no success number for the same model without the branch.
No trial counts, and no spread.
And the real-world sixty-one to eighty-one percent is fifteen people rating videos. No robot moved.

steps.say: Real robot runs exist: a generated cup pickup beside the real arm, then a pepper. Demonstrations, without a success rate.

scenes.text: Geometry can be taught through a branch you delete: the generator keeps the structure and pays nothing to run it.
scenes.say: The thing to keep: geometry can be taught through a branch you delete. The generator keeps the structure and pays nothing to run it.

recap: Pixels alone cannot fix depth or motion
A deleted branch teaches the middle block geometry
Better 3D; the success headline needs a fair baseline
scenes.say: To recap. Pixels alone cannot fix depth. A deleted branch teaches the model geometry. And the success headline still needs a fair baseline.
